correctness.rationale: Each input has a vertex scalar label vector a_u and arrow components b_i,uw. Modulo radical J, finite-field polynomial interpolation yields the whole k^V exactly when all a_u are pairwise distinct. For u!=w with delta=a_u-a_w nonzero, commutator components are images of ker(delta), dimension r-1. Necessity: if that image misses an arrow direction, quotient by its bimodule spans makes all input images commute but leaves a noncommuting algebra since an arrow has nonzero bracket with a vertex idempotent. Sufficiency: lift all vertex idempotents by polynomials, sandwich commutators, and obtain J_{uw} individually; quotient generation plus J generation gives A. Each restriction of a random r-to-m linear map to fixed hyperplane is onto in product_j(q^{r-1}-q^j) possibilities, and complementary direction gives q^m; blocks are independent. The count, probability, and generator-rank cutoff follow. Loopless hypothesis essential and singleton field v=1 no arrows has generator rank 0. Independently enumerated GF(2) word-span closure for parallel arrows, opposite arrows and disconnected diagrams; finite samples not proof.

originality.rationale: Iovanov–Sistko already classify maximal subalgebras of finite-dimensional quiver algebras via vertex merges and arrow hyperplanes. That could conceptually be used to derive generator obstructions but the inspected Theorem 4.1/Proposition 4.2 do not give a literal ordered r-tuple product over all arrow blocks. Sercombe–Shalev and Kravchenko–Mazur–Petrenko study more general random algebra generation, mostly bounds or semisimple cases; their named theorems do not tabulate these radical-square-zero quiver tuples. Residual risk is implicit enumeration from maximal-subalgebra theory or weakly indexed papers.
residual_risks: An implicit corollary of maximal-subalgebra theory or a specialized finite-quiver enumeration may predate this formula.
Loopful quivers and non-square-zero radicals are excluded; quotient commutativity obstruction fails if self-loop arrows survive.

value.rationale: Uniform finite-field generator counts, probabilities and minimal generator ranks are natural invariants of finite basic algebras. The exact formula handles every loopless directed multiquiver (including disconnected, parallel, reverse and cycles) and cleanly separates vertex-label collision from insufficient arrow-space rank. This general family classification is substantially broader than isolated hand computations.
